did_you_know.text: Did you know? Daniel 12 opens by describing Michael as “the great prince,” who stands watch over his people; in a time of distress, everyone whose name is found written in the book will be saved.
Did you know? The verse describes many of those who “sleep in the dust of the earth” awakening, with their destinies divided between everlasting life and disgrace and everlasting contempt.
Did you know? The wise are described as shining like the brightness of the sky, and those who lead many to righteousness are compared to stars shining forever and ever.
Did you know? Daniel is commanded to shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end; the same verse also says: “Many will go here and there, and knowledge will increase.”
Did you know? Two additional figures appear in the vision, one on each side of the river, after the description of the man dressed in linen.
Did you know? One of those standing beside the river asks the man dressed in linen, “How long will it be until the end of these wonders?” Thus, the question of when the vision will end is introduced.

Did you know? The man dressed in linen swears by the One who lives forever that the end will come after “a time, times, and half a time,” and that when the power of the holy people has been completely shattered, all these things will be finished.
Did you know? Daniel testifies that he heard the words but did not understand them, so he asked, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”
Did you know? According to the verse, many will be purified, cleansed, and refined; the wicked will not understand, but the wise will understand.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, two counts of days are mentioned: 1,290 days from the removal of the regular offering and the setting up of the abomination of desolation, followed by an additional 1,335 days; the verse does not explain their precise meaning here.
